chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Salma, the servant of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, narrated to me. She said: The hair of the wives of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was arranged in braids at the front of their heads, so a small amount of water used to suffice them. But as for women now, it is appropriate for them to use water thoroughly.

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is appropriate for her now to perform istibra' by urinating before ghusl. If that is not possible for her, then there is nothing upon her. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَشْعَارُ: the hair strands of the women المذكور in the report
key_terms.بِٱلْبَوْلِ: by urinating, here in the context of istibra' before ghusl
key_terms.قُرُونَ: braids or hair-twists gathered on the head
key_terms.ٱلنِّسَاءُ: women, specifically in reference to their purification practice

ai.seo_question: How should women perform ghusl in cases of janabah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling related to ghusl for women, noting that the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله had hairstyles that allowed a small amount of water to suffice. It also indicates that women in later times should apply water more thoroughly, and al-Shaykh adds that urinating before ghusl is recommended for istibra', though omission of that carries no liability.
